docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Lövell is an application for Electronically-Assisted Visual Astronomy.

It is built on the LÖVE 2D platform, using Lua as a scripting language running under LuaJit.

Lövell owes its existence to the amazing application Jocular, by @MartinCooke, and, to some extent, its successor, Canisp. The main display looks a bit like Canisp, the DSO and observations catalogues are lifted almost directly from Jocular (translated from Python to Lua.)

The novel thing about Lövell is that the image processing workflow is performed almost entirely within the GPU using code written in Open GL Shader Language. This makes it fast... most post-stack operations are performed within one video frame update (typically 1/60 second) so all interactive adjustments intensity / colour / filtering happen almost instantly.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
• download the appropriate (Mac or PC) image of LÖVE (https://love2d.org/#download)
  • install it, per the relevant instructions
  • download the Lövell.love file from this repository

docs.title: Quick tour
docs.text:
• click on the Lövell.love file (or drop onto the LÖVE app) to run it
  • drop a folder containing raw 16-bit FITS files onto the app window

docs.title: Main display
docs.text:
The main display shows a stacked image with controls for adjustments and an information panel. Most buttons are drop-down menus (which remain pinned if clicked rather than hovered.)

  • Channel: LRGB menu views LRGB / Mono / Inverted / Red / Green / Blue channels individually
  • Hyper is one of several stretch functions MidTone / Asinh / Hyper / Linear / Log / Gamma / ...
  • Luminance menu drops down to show additional gradient / vignette / white point sliders
  • background / stretch are the main luminance controls (right- or shift- click set to default)
  • RGB* menu also includes Hubble (SHO) and possibly other colour processing options
  • Chroma menu drops down to show additional tint / SCNR (green) sliders
  • saturation / temperature are the main chrominance controls for the RGB option
  • SynthL / Balance / Bilateral / Sharpen / CLAHE / etc. are controls for optional processing plugins
  • Prestack / Stack menus give options for those stages of processing
  • Databases (shown dropped down) gives access to various catalogs, etc.
  • mouse wheel / trackpad scroll zooms the display
  • click and drag moves the display
  • click on Eyepiece.. to switch to Landscape.. display, and vice versa
  • hover over eyepiece ring to activate image rotation, click and drag to change
  • enter object name in field on top right to search DSO catalogue

docs.title: DSO / Observation list
docs.text:
Some 40,000 objects of interest. Close button returns to main display.

  • click on column names to sort
  • text or numeric expressions in filter boxes to select subsets
  • click, shift-click, option/control-click to (de)select multiple items
  • right click on image to show pop-up menu of DSO / Observations / Watch list / View stack
  • scroll control to forward time by up to 24 hours, updating object positions in Az, Alt, etc...

docs.title: View stack/subs
docs.text:
View all the subs in sequence, show detected and matched stars. Close button returns to main display.

  • mouse wheel / trackpad to scroll through subs
  • Stretch applies a variable screen stretch to the display
  • Play button animates sequence of subs
  • rate control changes speed
  • Blink toggles between adjacent subs
  • Show stars indicates detected stars (in blue) and those matched for alignment (orange)

docs.title: Plugin architecture
docs.text: Most processing steps have been implemented in a modular plugin architecture which allows for (relatively) easy extensions. Each plugin is a classic MVC (model-view-control) structure containing its own controls, GUI, processing (probably implemented as a GLSL shader plus Lua code), and brief documentation.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Much of Lövell's functionality is implemented as separate processing modules called plugins. There are of two types: Static or Dynamic. There is a separate Plugin workflow editor page, which allows dynamic plugins to be (de)selected and placed in order into the post-stack workflow, appearing as dropdown menus on the main display page.

docs.title: Static Plugins
docs.text: Static plugins are part of the system workflow and, as such, are permanently installed

docs.title: Luminance
docs.text:
Luminance processing for both one-shot colour (OSC) and mono images (filtered or otherwise).

A number of different classical stretch functions are available from the strtch menu.

Background level and Stretch are visible at the top level if drop-down menu is split.

Gradient, Vignetting, and White point controls are available on the drop-down menu.

Vignetting adjustment is particularly valuable for wide-angle (short F-ratio) systems when a master flat is not available.

docs.title: RGB
docs.text:
RGB processing for both one-shot colour (OSC) and filtered mono images.

Saturation and Temperature (Blue : Yellow balance) are visible at the top level if drop-down menu is split.

Tint (Green : Magenta balance) and SCNR (Subtractive Chromatic Noise Reduction - Green) controls are available on the drop-down menu.

docs.title: Hubble
docs.text:
HUBBLE (pseudo-SHO) based on Bill Blanshan's "Narrowband Normalization" PixInsight code.

This treats RGB channels as HSO and swizzles them to be SHO ordered.

The controls are specfic to his process and more details can be found online, but feel free to experiment, the names are fairly self-explanatory.

docs.title: Dynamic Plugins
docs.text: Dynamic plugins may be picked to appear in the post-stack wrofklow processing chain.

docs.title: Generalised Hyperbolic Stretch (GHS)
docs.text:
• D (Stretch Factor): Controls the magnitude of the localized contrast boost around SP (D≥0).
  • b (Local Intensity): Controls how rapidly the gain drops off moving away from SP (b>0).
  • SP (Symmetry point): The pixel intensity value where contrast amplification is centered and maximal (0≤SP≤1).
  • D, b, and SP are visible at the top level if drop-down menu is split.

docs.title: Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Enhancement (CLAHE)
docs.text:
Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalisation.

This is a multi-scale implementation with individual strength and contrast limits.

The three scales correspond to structures of around 4, 8, and 32 pixels.]]

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: There are keyboard shortcuts for a number of different actions. Some of them work from any page, others are specific to a particular one.

docs.title: Global Shortcuts
docs.text:
!!! note ESC key returns to the main display from any page

Command- or Ctrl- depending on operating system:

⌘-Key Action C Calibration masters database D DSO database E Eyepiece mode F FITS headers L Landscape mode O Observations database P Plugin workflow editor S Settings page V View stack of subs

docs.title: Page-dependent Shortcuts
docs.text: ⌘-Key Action T Toggle between Eyepiece and Landscape mode 7 Scale to fill screen, possibly cropping one axis 8 Scale to fill screen, possibly leaving a margin 9 Fit to margins between control and information panels 0 Full size - one image pixel is one screen pixel + Zoom in – Zoom out . Rotate_to_zero / Rotate_clockwise, +90º \ Rotate_anticlockwise, -90º
